summary.headline: Syrma SGS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR1,477 crore at 11.9% operating EBITDA margin; FY27 EBITDA guided to INR700 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: consolidated revenue INR1,477 crore (+56% YoY, +16% QoQ), operating EBITDA INR174 crore (+51% YoY) at 11.9% margin, and PAT INR119 crore (+67% YoY). FY26 revenue reached INR4,857 crore (+27%), operating EBITDA INR545 crore (+68%, margin 11.3%), and the company moved to a net cash position of INR467 crore. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 30-35%, operating EBITDA margin of 10-10.5% (said to be conservative) and EBITDA of about INR700 crore, and is investing in a large PCB project. The Ksolare acquisition via the Premier Energies JV was dropped, and a greenfield renewable-inverter plan is being evaluated instead.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 31% of Q4 revenue; grew about 30% in FY26 including Elcome. Growth expected from power management, UPS and industrial electronics; about 24% of order book.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: 26% of Q4 revenue; about 31% of FY26 revenue (INR1,452 crore). Management caps it below 35% and pegs it near 30%, growing about 8-10% in FY27; about 30% of order book.

segments.name: Auto
segments.commentary: 24% of Q4 revenue; grew 39% in FY26. Auto exports crossed INR125 crore; about 29% of order book; FY27 growth expected to be mainly domestic.

segments.name: Healthcare (MedTech)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% in FY26 from INR291 crore to INR395 crore; management expects it to exceed INR500 crore in FY27. About 5% of order book.

segments.name: IT and railways
segments.commentary: Grew 182% YoY in Q4 and 74% in FY26; annualised revenue rose from about INR240 crore to INR476 crore. IT covers laptop, motherboard and memory products. About 11% of order book; management expects 30-40% growth going forward.

segments.name: ODM
segments.commentary: Revenue rose about 80% from INR453 crore to INR825 crore in FY26; share about 17% of revenue versus 12% a year earlier.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR1,200 crore+ in FY26 (24-25% of revenue), up 41%; Q4 run rate about INR125 crore per month. FY27 target about INR1,500 crore (20-30% growth).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-35%; management says the blended growth will be near 30-35% with individual verticals ranging from about 28% to 35%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 10.5-11% (earlier stated as at least 10-10.5%), kept conservative despite FY26 margin of about 12%.
Targeting about INR700 crore of EBITDA in FY27, a 30% absolute increase per management.
FY27 exports targeted at about INR1,500 crore; FY27 capex of INR100-150 crore organic plus PCB project spend.
FY28 onwards, PCB business to add incremental revenue (management cites possibly INR300-700 crore); FY28 growth expected above 30-35%.
Working capital days to be pushed down further, but management said it will not chase growth at the expense of working capital.
capex_capacity: PCB multilayer line project: about $90 million (INR800 crore) over multiple years, in two phases. Phase 1 INR400 crore, of which about INR50 crore was spent in FY26, about INR250 crore planned in FY27 and INR100 crore in FY28. Phase 2 runs into mid-FY29.

Commissioning of the first PCB phase expected towards the end of FY27 or start of FY28; partial government incentive claims thereafter, with at least a one-year lag. Management says the subsidy is expected at 50-60% of the spend.
ECMS approvals received for CCL (copper clad laminate), HDI and flex PCB; about INR800 crore capex expected to be executed between FY28 and FY30.
FY26 capex was about INR140 crore; FY27 organic capex planned at INR100-150 crore.
Real-time monitoring system being rolled out across assembly lines in phases; management reports a 5-7% improvement in operational efficiency so far.

Renewable energy/inverter: Ksolare acquisition via Premier Energies JV dropped after the seller did not meet conditions precedent; minimal expense charged to P&L. Management now plans a greenfield project and is evaluating technology partner proposals, with an update expected in the coming quarter.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR6,600 crore at March-end 2026 (auto 29%, consumer 30%, industrial 24%, healthcare 5%, IT and railways 11%). Net addition of about INR200 crore after Q4 deliveries; Elcome is about 5% of the order book.
Q4 run rate is about INR500 crore per month. Management says the second half is seasonally stronger than the first half.
Customer concentration (FY26): top 5 about 34% of revenue, top 10 about 47%, top 20 about 63%.
32 new customers onboarded in FY26 (about 7 in industrial). Management says they could add about INR1,000 crore to FY26 revenue and about INR2,500 crore per year long-term.

Pass-through clauses exist in customer contracts for metal and logistics cost variation, but recovery is negotiated and is not immediate. Management expects partial cost increases to be offset by better buying and efficiency, with costs shared across vendor, customer and end consumer.

Smart metering: about INR250-260 crore of revenue in FY26, with a gross material margin of about 12-15%; management is being selective given working capital intensity. Elcome has a 3-6 month working capital cycle, and defence is a high-margin ODM business.

Competition: management said competitive intensity will rise as Tier-2 global EMS players and large Indian groups enter; it claims a cost advantage. Global addressable market is cited at over $600 million, against about $500 million of current revenue.
EU FTA: about a 1-1.5% duty benefit in select cases; management says the longer-term impact is positive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex profile for the PCB and other projects, and when do the government incentives start?
qa_highlights.answer: PCB phase 1 is INR400 crore (INR250 crore in FY27, INR100 crore in FY28). Organic capex is INR100-150 crore a year. Commissioning is expected towards the end of FY27 or the start of FY28, with incentives claimed in part and typically lagging by a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw-material and inflation outlook, and how are costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal prices, logistics and shipping routes are affected by the Middle East crisis. Contracts have pass-through clauses but recovery is negotiated and takes time. Management says better buying and efficiency can offset part of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 margin guided at 10.5-11% when Q4 was 11.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is being conservative given geopolitics, shipping and metal-price volatility. It says it prefers to beat its guidance and will revise it at the Q1 call if conditions stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company fund the PCB capex without running short of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the project will be funded through debt, internal accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution, with subsidies of 50-60% expected. It says cash will not fall short over the project life. Balance-sheet cash is INR829 crore against a net cash position of INR470 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth comes from market share gains versus industry growth, and how does the PCB business affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the growth to market share and wallet-share gains, portfolio expansion (MedTech, defence) and larger customer contracts. PCB revenue is incremental, starting in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EU and export outlook, and what is the PLI benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Export guidance is INR1,500 crore for FY27, about 25-30% growth. Management expects at least 25% growth over the coming years. FY26 gross PLI was about INR80 crore and net about INR38 crore; Q4 net PLI was about INR10-12 crore.

risks_watch: FY27 margin guide of 10.5-11% sits below the 11.9% Q4 and about 12% FY26 margin; management cites metal prices, shipping routes and the Middle East disruption, and says it will revise at the Q1 FY27 call if conditions stabilise.
Pass-through of metal and logistics cost increases is negotiated, not immediate; the lag and the share borne by Syrma, customers and end consumers remain unquantified.

PCB project: about INR800 crore capex, with INR250 crore planned in FY27; commissioning is expected towards end-FY27 or start-FY28, and government subsidy claims lag by at least a year. Funding relies on debt, accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution; the analyst's cash-shortfall concern was answered but not quantified.

Working capital at 63 days (58 ex-Elcome); management will not chase growth at the expense of working capital, but Elcome and defence carry 3-6 month cycles, and smart metering is being limited for the same reason.

Order book grew only about INR200 crore net in Q4 to about INR6,600 crore; the analyst noted it covers about 24% of the 30-35% growth target on its own, and management said the order book is continuously refreshed, with many orders running only 3-6 months.
Rising competition from Tier-2 global EMS players and large Indian groups; management says competitive intensity will increase.
Ksolare acquisition dropped; a greenfield renewable inverter project is being evaluated, with technology partner choice and an update expected in the coming quarter.
key_quotes: We would like to err on the side of caution and we have guided 10.5% to 11% margin despite having delivered 12% margin.
We are willing to sacrifice top line growth if the working capital cycle is elongated. We are not chasing growth at the expense of working capital cycle.
We are competing with the Tier 2 level global EMS companies. Competition -- competitive intensity would increase.
We'll not fall short of cash. You see, what we spent, we have projected about $40 million, which is about INR400 crores or whatever, INR360 crores, INR400 crores for the current year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the FY27 revenue and EBITDA targets, but deliberately cautious on margin, guiding 10.5-11% against a roughly 12% run-rate and citing geopolitics and metal costs. Evasive on PCB funding detail, the renewable-energy project and the margin cushion; several answers were deferred to later quarters.

adds.what: PCB multilayer line project Phase 1 (INR400 crore of INR800 crore total PCB plan), commissioning expected towards end FY27 or start FY28
ECMS-approved CCL, HDI and flex PCB capacity, about INR800 crore capex to be executed FY28-FY30
Greenfield renewable-energy/inverter project (Ksolare JV dropped); technology partner under evaluation, no capex quantified

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 30-35% (midpoint 32.5%), backed by an INR6,600 crore order book (about +200 crore net addition after Q4), 32 new customers and exports target of INR1,500 crore+, while the main new capacity (PCB Phase 1, INR400 crore) only commissions around end-FY27, so near-term growth rests on existing capacity and order book.
